about: THE PORTS OF 793 - the trading places a ship can put in at. Names as then (Latin of the charters where that is what survives); modern place; realm in 793 (ids for realms_793.json, to come); region (a trade region: what it makes and wants is in goods_793.json); county (an id from Build/Guide/lands_793.json where there is one); kind; landing (beach, jetty, quay, riverbank); size 1 (a landing) to 5 (a great emporium) - how many buildings its blockout gets; from/to: years it trades (0 = before the game / no end); (?) uncertain. Inland river ports get their water with the river bake. Edit freely: the game reads this file.

ports.name: Dorestat
ports.note: The greatest emporium of the north, where the Kromme Rijn leaves the Lek; a kilometre of jetties; the king's toll and mint.

ports.name: Traiectum
ports.note: Willibrord's see and the church of Saint Martin, on the Rhine where the Vecht leaves it north.

ports.name: Walichrum
ports.note: An emporium on the dunes of Walcheren at the Scheldt mouth, later lost to the sea.

ports.name: Witla
ports.note: A lost trading place at the mouth of the Maas, burned in 836 (?).

ports.name: Medemelacha
ports.note: West Frisian trading place on the Almere shore, on the inland route north from Dorestad.

ports.name: Winaldum
ports.note: A great terp in Westergo, seat of Frisian lords (?).

ports.name: Doccinga
ports.note: Terp village in Oostergo, where Boniface was killed in 754.

ports.name: Emuthon
ports.note: A trading terp at the mouth of the Ems.

ports.name: Daventre
ports.note: Lebuinus's church on the IJssel, the road east to the Saxons.

ports.name: Noviomagus
ports.note: The king's palace above the Waal.

ports.name: Quentovic
ports.note: The Franks' Channel emporium on the Canche; the king's toll, the crossing to the English.

ports.name: Rotomagus
ports.note: Archbishop's city on the Seine, the tide's reach.

ports.name: Parisius
ports.note: The Seine city; the great autumn fair of Saint-Denis draws English and Frisian merchants.

ports.name: Ganda
ports.note: The abbeys of Saint Bavo and Saint Peter where the Lys meets the Scheldt.

ports.name: Andoverpis
ports.note: A fort and landing on the Scheldt.

ports.name: Colonia
ports.note: The old Roman city on the Rhine, an archbishop's see; wine and Rhenish pottery.

ports.name: Mogontia
ports.note: Archbishop's city at the Main's mouth; Frisian merchants have their own quarter.

ports.name: Diusburg
ports.note: A trading place on the Rhine at the Ruhr's mouth.

ports.name: Lundenwic
ports.note: Bede's 'mart of many peoples': the wic on the Strand, ships beached on the Thames foreshore.

ports.name: Hamwic
ports.note: Wessex's emporium on the Itchen, trading with Quentovic and the Seine.

ports.name: Gipeswic
ports.note: The East Angles' wic on the Orwell, its potters' Ipswich ware sold up the coast.

ports.name: Eoforwic
ports.note: Northumbria's city: the minster, Alcuin's school, and the wic where the Foss meets the Ouse.

ports.name: Serræ
ports.note: A toll place on the Wantsum channel, where ships cut inside Thanet.

ports.name: Fordwic
ports.note: Canterbury's landing on the Stour.

ports.name: Dofras
ports.note: The short crossing to the Franks.

ports.name: Lindisfarena
ports.note: Cuthbert's holy island; the northmen fall on it on 8 June 793.

ports.name: Bebbanburg
ports.note: The Northumbrian kings' rock fortress on the coast.

ports.name: Gyrwe
ports.note: Bede's monastery on the Tyne (with Wearmouth).

ports.name: Streonæshalch
ports.note: Hild's abbey on the cliff above the Esk.

ports.name: Dommoc
ports.note: The East Angles' bishop's see on the coast (?).

ports.name: Legacæstir
ports.note: The old legionary town on the Dee, facing Wales and Ireland.

ports.name: Hī
ports.note: Columba's island; the northmen come in 795.

ports.name: Duiblinn
ports.note: A church by the black pool on the Liffey; the longphort comes in 841.

ports.name: Ripa
ports.note: The Danes' oldest market town, on the Ribe river behind the Wadden: beads, combs, wine and Frisian cloth.

ports.name: Sliesthorp
ports.note: A market at the head of the Schlei, where the road crosses to the Eider; it grows when Godfred moves Reric's merchants here in 808.

ports.name: Reric
ports.note: The Obodrites' emporium; Godfred burns it and takes its merchants to Sliesthorp in 808.

ports.name: Skíringssalr
ports.note: Vestfold's market town (from about 800, (?) earlier): Ohthere sails here from Hålogaland.

ports.name: Birka
ports.note: The Svear's market town on an island in the bay (the sea came in further then).

ports.name: Helgö
ports.note: An older craft and trading place, giving way to Birka.

ports.name: Uppsalir
ports.note: The Svear kings' seat and temple, up the Fyris river.

ports.name: Paviken
ports.note: A Gotland harbour market of shipwrights and smiths.

ports.name: Áhús
ports.note: A trading place at the Helge river mouth in Skåne.

ports.name: Truso
ports.note: The Prussians' amber market on Lake Drużno; Wulfstan sails here from Hedeby.

ports.name: Grobiņa
ports.note: A Scandinavian settlement among the Curonians.

ports.name: Aldeigjuborg
ports.note: The gate to the east on the Volkhov: furs going west, dirhams coming north.

ports.name: Ögvaldsnes
ports.note: A king's seat on the Karmsund, the sheltered way north along the coast.

ports.name: Hleiðr
ports.note: The Skjöldung kings' hall, up the Roskilde fjord.

ports.name: Namnetis
ports.note: The Loire city at the Breton march: salt and wine.

ports.name: Herio
ports.note: Saint Philibert's island monastery and its salt pans; raided in 799.

ports.name: Burdigala
ports.note: The Garonne city of Aquitaine: wine.
